report.summary: Test/CI-only change. Ran the changed Worker suites (ops.test.ts + workspace-rpc.test.ts: 199/199 pass) and scripts/ci-changes.test.ts (5/5 pass). The docs-only classifier fails closed for a missing, zero, invalid or unreachable base, an empty diff, workflow_dispatch, a failed fetch, any code or config path and the code side of a rename. The docs-only path keeps the required check job and runs the pinned oxlint/oxfmt, whose configs need no node_modules. Turbo inputs: Worker code and Worker tests import nothing from src/ui or src/routes; UI/component inputs include test/ui fixtures and storage-stub; the fixture build outputs (test/web/dist, test/browser/dist) match Vite's default outDir for each root; only tempod has a build script, so replacing ^build with ^transit drops nothing the tests need. GitHub spies and the Date.now spy stay in sequential groups; held daemon fakes register cleanup on their own test context. One non-blocking issue: a concurrent ops test changes the shared STEP_LIMITS table. Playwright suites were not run locally because they write build output into the repo; their new selectors exist in the UI source.

findings.text: The 'aborts a step at its timeout' test changes the shared STEP_LIMITS table and is now inside describe.concurrent("step runner rules"). The four other cases in that group run seedWs/readyWs, whose create op runs settings.read with the 300 ms limit while this test runs. On a loaded runner, a slow fake reply would count as a failed attempt and add retries and backoff to unrelated cases. This conflicts with AGENTS.md: 'Keep global clock/GitHub mock groups sequential'. The test passed locally, so this is not shown to fail; moving this one test to a sequential group would remove the risk.

evidence.why: STEP_LIMITS is a module-level table shared with the Durable Object runner (the test depends on that to get TEMPOD_TIMEOUT). The test sits in a describe.concurrent group with maxConcurrency 4, so the other cases see the shortened timeout while it runs.

checked.risk: Real contracts (Vitest concurrent test context, Playwright projects and tags, Turbo transit and inputs, GitHub Actions outputs, git fetch in a shallow clone)
Failure paths / fail-closed docs-only classification and CI sequencing
Tests: concurrency, shared globals, spies, cleanup, assertions
Build/runtime environment and cache correctness (Turbo inputs covering imports, fixture outputs)
Spec and repository rules (CI.md, 06 Build Plan, AGENTS.md)
